item.title: Luigi Mangione in talks about possible guilty plea with court date today, sources say
item.description: Luigi Mangione, accused in the 2024 killing of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson, is in discussions about a possible plea deal on federal charges, sources familiar with the matter told CBS News.

item.title: Count Binface wins hearts, if not the election, in bid to defeat Trump ally
item.description: Count Binface, a satirical candidate who's become a mainstay in recent U.K. elections, achieved his greatest success yet.

item.title: Trump asks Supreme Court to intervene in White House ballroom legal fight
item.description: The Trump administration asked the Supreme Court to intervene in the legal battle over President Trump's White House ballroom.

item.title: Paintings worth $10 million that were stolen in 3-minute heist are recovered
item.description: The recovered works are valued at more than $10 million.

item.title: 2 killed as Apache helicopter from Fort Hood crashes in Salado, Texas
item.description: Two soldiers aboard an AH-64 Apache attack helicopter based out of Fort Hood were killed in a crash on Wednesday, according to local authorities and the Army.

item.title: UAE accuses Iran of Hormuz attacks as Vance says cheap gas is "goal number one"
item.description: The UAE accuses Iran of attacking two vessels in the Strait of Hormuz as Vance says cheap oil and gas is "goal number one" from the war.

item.title: New effort to add Trump's name on outside of Kennedy Center could face legal challenges
item.description: The Kennedy Center board members, most of whom were appointed by President Trump, voted on Thursday to add an inscription to the building under the Kennedy Center sign that says the building was "restored and renovated by President Donald J. Trump." The new effort to add the president's name could face legal pushback. Nancy Cordes explains.

item.title: Dad of USS Lincoln sailor worries about crew as deployment stretches on
item.description: The USS Abraham Lincoln has been at sea for nine months, and sailors have maintained a grueling pace amid the war in Iran.

item.title: AI is driving up consumer prices. That won't stop anytime soon.
item.description: Surging AI investment is pushing up the cost of smartphones and other gadgets, according to analysts. Here's why.

item.title: Hawaii under a hurricane warning as Tropical Storm Lala takes aim
item.description: Tropical Storm Lala could bring heavy rain, high winds and dangerous surf and rip currents to the Hawaiian Islands as a hurricane this weekend, forecasters say.

item.title: USS Washington aircraft carrier heads to Middle East to replace USS Lincoln
item.description: The USS George Washington aircraft carrier departed Vietnam last week and is headed to the Middle East to replace the USS Abraham Lincoln, according to a U.S. official.

item.title: Unemployed women taking GLP-1 drugs more likely to get hired, study claims
item.description: A study on the use of GLP-1 drugs shows they may be helping some women get ahead in their careers. CBS MoneyWatch reporter Megan Cerullo has more.

item.title: Flock CEO reacts to brutal misuse allegations involving his shocking technology
item.description: Flock CEO Garrett Langley sat down with CBS News' Anna Schecter and discussed allegations of the technology's misuse by law enforcement.

item.title: Teen caught on video kicking sea lion pleads guilty, faces prison time
item.description: Tyler Muehl, 18, pleaded guilty in federal court after a viral video captured him attacking the sea lion at La Jolla Cove.

item.title: Poland claims it stopped a Russian plan to kill a Ukrainian-American citizen in Warsaw
item.description: Poland is claiming that it thwarted a Russian plot to kill a Ukrainian-American citizen in Warsaw. "He was inconvenient from the point of view of the Putin regime," Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said. CBS News' Ramy Inocencio reports.

item.title: News expected in Luigi Mangione federal case. Here's what to know.
item.description: Luigi Mangione may plead guilty as part of an agreement with federal prosecutors, sources tell CBS News. Katrina Kaufman reports.

item.title: USS Abraham Lincoln faces allegations of food shortages, plumbing issues and mental health crises
item.description: Democrats are demanding answers as allegations about the conditions aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln continue to emerge. CBS News' Charlie D'Agata reports.

item.title: Extreme weather slams the Midwest and in Indiana floodwaters are rising again
item.description: The Midwest is bracing for more extreme weather after flooding inundated entire streets in some areas. CBS News' Ian Lee reports.

item.title: Some schools are scaling back on how much they rely on screens in the classroom
item.description: As students across the country head back to the classroom, some schools, educators and parents are rethinking how much they utilize technology and screen time. Nicole Valdes has more.

item.title: Flock CEO apologizes, outlines changes amid claims its data was misused by police in some cases
item.description: Flock CEO Garrett Langley apologized in an interview with CBS News amid claims the surveillance company's license plate readers have been misused by some police officers. Langley also addressed new safety measures that were recently announced. Anna Schecter reports.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy's journal entries read in court after emotional moments in murder trial
item.description: Lindsay Clancy, the Massachusetts woman in court for the alleged murder of her three children, heard parts of her journal being read out as part of the proceedings. This comes after an emotional week that included autopsy images of her children. Abby Patkin, a Boston.com reporter, joins CBS News with more details.

item.title: New details from NTSB explain why a Ryanair passenger was partially sucked out of window
item.description: The National Transportation Safety Board has released new details about what may have caused a window to shatter on a Ryanair flight, partially sucking a passenger out of the window. Kris Van Cleave reports.

item.title: American missionary kidnapped in Niger in October is freed, his group says
item.description: An American missionary who was kidnapped in Niger in October has been released, his organization says, adding that Kevin Rideout "is in good health in the care of U.S. officials."

item.title: 3 executions carried out in a single day, first time since 2010
item.description: Tennessee and Oklahoma executed inmates within 30 minutes of each other on Thursday, followed by Alabama later in the day.

item.title: They've survived 2 major earthquakes in Colombia and know what comes next
item.description: Colombia earthquake survivors are facing major loss and a yearslong road to recovery filled with grief and uncertainty. Here's what responders say will happen next.

item.title: Kennedy Center board votes to restore Trump's name on building
item.description: The Kennedy Center's board of trustees voted to add President Trump's name to the facade of the performing arts center, more than two months after a judge ordered its removal, according to a Democrat who sits on the center's board.

item.title: From the archives: "Off Campus" star Belmont Cameli donates his kidney (2018)
item.description: Before Belmont Cameli was a star on "Off Campus," he sparked a chain reaction of kindness back in 2018, when he was known as Philip Belmont Cameli. He was trying to donate his kidney to a childhood friend. They weren't a match, but he decided to make a donation anyway... to a stranger. Other donors followed and did the same. CBS News' Dean Reynolds covered this story on Feb. 28, 2018.

item.title: Cities propose new tactics to crack down on so-called "teen takeovers"
item.description: Large gatherings of young people, often spurred by online invites, can lead to violence and injuries, even death.

item.title: U.K. far-right leader Nigel Farage resigns as lawmaker in risky gamble
item.description: Populist British lawmaker Nigel Farage has resigned amid a financial scandal, but says he'll run in a snap election to reclaim his seat.

item.title: Murders plummeted more than 20% in U.S. in 2025, study shows
item.description: The 2025 national homicide rate might be the lowest recorded in the U.S. since 1900.
